discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munchen, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers predicted in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model, turning a central model of condensed-matter theory into a tunable laboratory system. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, the first clean realisation of a strongly correlated quantum phase with neutral atoms. This established the field of analogue quantum simulation. Bloch and Greiner went on to develop quantum-gas microscopes that image and control single atoms in many-body states. With these tools they observed antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localisation, string patterns and entanglement. Zoller's theory work set out the programme behind these experiments, from synthetic gauge fields to lattice gauge theories. Together their work made long-standing questions about correlated quantum matter directly testable in experiments. It now underpins a worldwide effort in quantum simulation and quantum technologies.
